column1: # G12 phase 5: multiple(n), the divisor atom of the numeric domain
# obtained by running both engines and requiring them to agree.
# A value is admitted when its exact value is an integer multiple of
# each divisor: an integer or 0d leaf by its own value, a float through
# its shortest spelling, since 0.3 is a multiple of 0.1 and the double
# Divisors accumulate as atoms, one per value and in value order, with
# no least common multiple made of them; canon writes them after neq.
# A divisor is a positive number, and multiple() takes exactly one.
# A whole divisor admits only whole numbers, so an interval holding none
# is empty when the atoms meet, as it is under the integer leaf; a
# fractional divisor makes no such claim.
# A count is not divisible here: len() refuses a divisor.
